_comment: One rule is switched off here. It is not a silent suppression: it carries a reason, and the property it protects is held by a test rather than by this entry.

_resolved.bootstrap.cp-authorization: Suppressed on 2026-08-01 and withdrawn the same day. The finding was a real false positive — the rule grepped for `$this->authorize(`, `Gate::`, `->can(`, `abort_unless`, `abort_if` and `authorizeResource`, and did not know `authorizeOrFail()`, Statamic's own guard on `Statamic\Http\Controllers\CP\Controller`. This addon routes through it deliberately, because `hasPermission()` crashes on eloquent-driver sites where the authenticated model is a plain App\Models\User. But a rule that fires on a correct addon is a broken rule, not a rule to switch off: it was fixed in the studio, so it is live again here and would catch a genuinely unguarded route. tests/Feature/CpWriteRouteAuthorizationTest.php proves the property independently — all 38 CP write routes answer 403 to a user without LeadHub permissions, and a new unguarded one fails there on the day it is added.
_resolved._note: Entries under _resolved are history, not configuration. addon-lint only reads `disable`.

_why.testing.addon-testcase: Deliberate, and it needs a decision rather than a quiet fix. Switching tests/TestCase.php to Statamic\Testing\AddonTestCase was attempted on 2026-08-01 and produced 201 failures out of 501. AddonTestCase mocks the Nav facade without an `extend` expectation, and — more fundamentally — its manifest wiring makes Statamic register the addon's own routes and listeners on top of the ones this TestCase mounts by hand, so every event-driven side effect fires twice (engagement scores came out doubled). The hand-rolled setup is not accidental: it boots the brand-context sibling before this addon, flips the storage driver from LEADHUB_DRIVER, swaps SQLite for MySQL from DB_DRIVER for the InnoDB key-length suite, purges the flat-file store between tests, and mounts the CP routes with SubstituteBindings so a sibling addon's Route::bind() collision is reproducible. Migrating to AddonTestCase means rebuilding all of that against core's ordering — a project, not a sweep item. Tracked for a separate pass.
